A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ABCD research work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The expanded v4 material can be reliably matched against v3, including relocated figures and the retained termination proof.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on mixtures of Gaussians, Sudoku, Pixel Maze, OGBench PointMaze, and QM9, with quantitative results and ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds text-to-image generation experiments, compute measurements, and analyses of temperature allocation and output diversity.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same main ABCD procedure. Appendix C.3 newly introduces and tests an Adaptive ABCD variant that redistributes particles across noise levels in proportion to their observed average rewards. This is a limited procedural addition, explicitly not adopted as the main method.

E1.justification: v4 adds 512×512 text-to-image generation using Stable Diffusion v1.5, animal prompts and human-instruction prompts, with compressibility, aesthetic, and human-preference objectives (Section 5.7; B.14–B.15). This substantially extends evaluation into a new output domain while retaining all earlier task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained benchmark comparisons is unchanged. Table 15 adds a direct comparison against the newly defined Adaptive ABCD variant. The image experiments use existing comparators Base Diffusion, BoN, and SoP; the newly cited reward-model papers are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: B.16 adds function-evaluation accounting per particle per step, supplementing wall-clock comparisons across retained tasks. New experiments introduce a 12-image-per-method evaluation protocol, three image-reward metrics, CLIP-based diversity measurement, and controlled temperature-pool-size comparisons. The existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; additional NFE reporting does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: C.2–C.4 add temperature-pool-granularity experiments, comparison with reward-weighted temperature allocation, and output-diversity analysis. B.15.1 adds image-generation case studies, and B.16 examines computational efficiency beyond wall-clock timing. Existing go-back and stopping analyses are retained; some Sudoku stopping-parameter material expands or redisplays comparisons already present in v3.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean/spread values and standard-deviation plots. v4 extends these reporting practices to additional results without introducing repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The performance and timing values in Tables 1–7 are retained, with NFE entries added to Tables 5–7. Tables 8–16 add image rewards, sensitivity results, variant comparisons, and diversity scores; for example, Table 9 reports ABCD aesthetic score 6.25 ± 0.09 at 288.42 seconds. Some image performance/timing pairs in Figure 7 do not match the corresponding appendix tables.

T1.justification: The diffusion and reward-guided-generation mathematics are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same assumptions, termination theorem, supporting lemmas, and proof arguments. The added empirical metrics do not introduce new formal theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive computation, cyclic refinement, exploration control, stopping, and improved efficiency across tasks. The image experiments provide additional support without redefining those core contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations concerning high-dimensional image applicability, temperature-pool diversity, and preservation of output multimodality. C.3 also explains retaining uniform allocation because reward-weighted allocation offers little benefit for its complexity. The original mechanism discussion and Section 6 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: B.14 adds image-generation implementation details: the pretrained backbone, prompt and scorer sources, N=4, K=1, J=4, go-back levels, κ=30, and 50-step jumpy denoising. These document the added experiments; existing hardware descriptions, retained-task implementation details, and resource-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds four references supporting the image experiments: Black et al. on diffusion reinforcement learning, LAION-Aesthetics, and the two Human Preference Score papers. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning against existing inference-time methods remain intact.

P1.justification: v4 adds experiment and appendix subsections, adjusts cross-references and heading capitalization, and revises author contribution/contact information and the publication footer. The existing introduction, method, limitations, and conclusion are substantially verbatim, so the expansion does not constitute extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v4 expands Figure 2 and adds image-reward curves, generated-image comparisons, and NFE plots in Figures 7 and 16–20. It also adds Tables 8–16 and NFE columns to Tables 5–7. These substantially expand the visual presentation; earlier figures are otherwise retained and mostly renumbered or relocated.

improvement.justification: NFE accounting in B.16 makes the central efficiency comparisons more auditable, while C.2–C.4 provide useful evidence about design choices and diversity. The image experiments also broaden empirical support. However, their 12-image evaluation and unexplained differences between Figure 7 and Tables 8–10 limit confidence in the new quantitative claims. The net gain is positive but qualified by these reporting weaknesses.
